messages:
maria: heads up — customer ACME reported weird behavior on embeddings cache. they claim ~30% of requests that should hit the cache are missing and some hits are returning wrong-dimension vectors. pasted their repro below. can someone take a look?

maria: customer payload (redacted):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-lite-512",
  "input": ["query A", "query B"]
}
```

maria: logs they shared (sanitized):
```
2026-02-20T15:22:11Z INFO cache.lookup key=acme-prefix::sha1(query A) -> MISS
2026-02-20T15:22:11Z INFO batch.prepare batch_id=bf9 model=redwood-embed-lite-512 size=2
2026-02-20T15:22:11Z INFO cache.insert key=acme-prefix::sha1(query A)#dim=1024 -> STORED
2026-02-20T15:22:11Z INFO response sent: dims=[1024,1024]
```

maria: customer insists they never used a 1024 model. they only have redwood-embed-lite-512 configured.

lena: hmm. two likely leads: 1) cache key doesn't include model version/dim so different models collide, 2) batching pipeline might be mixing requests from different clients or model variants into one batch and using the wrong model runtime.

sam: i asked for their request ids — they included two separate requests 6551 and 6552 sent ~10ms apart. their SDK uses a reuseable cache prefix header: `X-Embed-Cache-Prefix: acme-prefix`.

sam: quick repro i just did locally: i ran 2 clients, one targeting `redwood-embed-lite-512` and another `redwood-embed-pro-1024`, both using the same `X-Embed-Cache-Prefix`. when I sent the same input, the cache recorded `#dim=1024` after the pro batch ran. so if prefix doesn't encode model/dim, you get collisions.

maria: that matches the log where insert was `#dim=1024`. customer was probably running an A/B test and forgot to isolate the prefix per model.

taylor: thanks. two follow-ups: a) can we confirm server-side code includes `dim` in cache key? b) if not, is there a short-term mitigation for customers?

lena: current behaviour: cache key = `${prefix}::sha1(input)` by default. we append meta tags like `#dim=...` at write time for debugging but not used as part of lookup normalization. so lookup sees `acme-prefix::sha1(query A)` and hits any stored entry, even if stored vectors have different dims. that explains wrong-dim vectors being returned.

lena: short term mitigation options:
- recommend customers include model identifier in the prefix (e.g., `acme-prefix:redwood-embed-lite-512`).
- implement strict-keying toggle per-tenant that namespaces keys with model+dim on lookup and insert.
- reject mixed-dimension batches at batching layer (quick check).

maria: customer is currently experiencing production errors — they asked for a workaround we can push now.

taylor: i can push a change to the cache lookup to prefer entries that match stored `#dim` metadata when available. fallback to existing behaviour if no metadata. that should stop wrong-dim responses immediately without requiring SDK changes. low risk.

sam: quick POC patch in my branch:
```diff
- result = cache.get(prefix_key)
+ candidate = cache.get(prefix_key)
+ if candidate and candidate.meta.dim != expected_dim:
+   result = None
+ else:
+   result = candidate
```

sam: local tests show it prevents returning 1024 vectors for 512 requests, and reduces false-hits. perf impact minimal for single-key checks.

maria: can we deploy that as a hotfix? customer wants a config flag too so they can opt in.

ops-bot: deploy request created: DR-3251 by taylor — patch to cache strict-dim lookup.

taylor: i'll cut a canary to prod in staging region now, 15min window.

support-bot: ticket #12345 updated — workaround posted to customer: "please include model identifier in your cache prefix (e.g., prefix:model-name) until we enable strict-dim lookup for your org."

lena: longer-term: we should change the canonical cache key to include model id and quantization/dim fingerprint so collisions are impossible. plus validations in the batching queue to reject mixing models with different dims. i'll draft an RFC.

maria: customer also reported some throughput spikes when cache miss storms happen after deploy. might be related: their SDK batches inputs aggressively across threads and occasionally merges requests from different model configs into the same batch.

sam: added a repro where a single client thread uses a shared batcher and switches model param between requests — it creates mixed batches. code snippet from their SDK (simplified):
```js
// pseudo
batcher.add({input: 'a', model: 'lite-512'})
batcher.add({input: 'b', model: 'pro-1024'})
// batcher blindly groups by time window not model
```

lena: short term fix: batcher should group by model signature first, then time window. i'll add as acceptance criteria for the batching refactor.

maria: customer confirmed they can stage the prefix change on their side; they'd still like our hotfix to avoid a rollout across many microservices.

taylor: canary looks green for 10 minutes. deploying to rest of prod in 5. will keep rollback window open.

ops-bot: deployment DR-3251 promoted to prod by taylor at 2026-02-20T16:05:12Z — no errors.

maria: customer accepted the workaround and we'll follow up with a config change and RFC. closing for now but filing a postmortem note.

sam: note for docs: add "cache prefix best practices" to embeddings guide: always include model id and env marker in prefix.

lena: RFC draft in #eng-ml next week.

maria: thanks everyone. cc @support-bot please ping me if any regressions. :thumbsup:
